newsitem.title: JORDAN: EU envoy says working to avoid Mideast violence.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy says working to avoid Mideast violence.

text.p: Europe's Middle East peace envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos said on Tuesday the European Union was working to avoid violence in the region after Israel's decision to build settlements around Arab East Jerusalem.

"We have been in close contact with the Palestinians and we have been in contact with the Israeli authorities...to try to avoid decisions (that) can undermine the goodwill between the parties and the peace process," Moratinos told reporters after talks with Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.
Arab states have condemned Israel's decision to build 6,500 Jewish homes in Jabal Abu Ghneim, known in Hebrew as Har Homa, as a violation of its self-rule accord with Palestinians.
"We are not in favour of building settlements," said Moratinos, adding the peace process had reached "a very difficult moment".

"When you are in diplomacy you want to avoid violence so I think the best hope for everybody and the peace process itself is to avoid violence and we hope and we are working to avoid violence," he said.

Anger against Israeli settlement policy in Jerusalem has been mounting among Palestinians. The projects complete a circle of Jewish settlements around East Jerusalem which Israel began building after it captured the city in the 1967 Middle East war.
Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers died in gun battles after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened a tourist tunnel near Islamic holy shrines in Jerusalem in September.
Moratinos said he had told Kabariti about his plans to visit Damascus and revive talks between Israel and Syria which have been on hold for a year.

Syria says Israel's previous Labour government, which lost to Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud Party in elections last May, had agreed to withdraw from the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.
Moratinos' visit to Jordan coincided with Middle East trips by two European foreign ministers.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette was in Jerusalem for talks with Israeli officials and his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel was due in Amman on Tuesday to meet King Hussein for talks on the Middle East peace process and economic assistance to Jordan.
